By advocating for this strategic redirection, the plan positioned utilities to navigate and grow in the changing energy landscape, leveraging opportunities for revenue generation through firm capacity, operating reserves, and the provision of energy. This business plan also addressed the challenges and opportunities presented by the evolving energy sector dynamics. As DERs become more prevalent, traditional utility models that rely heavily on energy sales are becoming less viable. The plan, therefore, proposed innovative business models that incorporate DERs into wholesale markets and utility planning, ensuring long-term sustainability and profitability. It stressed the need for utilities to adapt to these changes by focusing on network management and ancillary services, thereby securing their position in a rapidly evolving energy ecosystem. PacifiCorp and project team members collaborated in sessions to discuss the approach to the business model plan including meeting with the market policy and analytics department to engage the knowledge and expertise for strategic guidance on this task. In its current state, the plan for the business model includes five core components: 13 1. Strategic Aggregation and Deployment of DERs. As part of the business model plan, the operational and technological frameworks are essential for effective DER aggregation. This includes the development of digital platforms for real-time management, the establishment of standardized communication protocols, and the implementation of advanced forecasting tools. Additionally, strategies for optimal DER deployment in wholesale markets are crucial. These strategies should take into account pricing models and the necessary investments in grid infrastructure to support DER integration. 2. Facilitation of DERs as Non-Wires Alternatives (NWAs). As part of the business model plan, advanced grid analytics and GIS were to be utilized to identify locations where other DERs can serve as effective NWAs, specifically targeting areas experiencing congestion, aging infrastructure, or reliability risks. To guide the selection of NWA projects effectively, a comprehensive evaluation framework is essential. This framework should incorporate lifecycle cost analysis, grid impact simulations, and environmental assessments to ensure a thorough and informed decision-making process. 3. Operational Coordination Models for TSO-DSO. As part of the business model plan, the merits and challenges of centralized versus layered structures for enhancing grid reliability and operational efficiency were to be investigated. It includes case studies and simulations to illustrate potential challenges and solutions. The document advocates for hybrid Distribution System Operator (DSO) models that amalgamate the strengths of both centralized and layered approaches. These models are to be supported by suitable technological and regulatory frameworks to ensure their effectiveness and sustainability. 4. Integration into the Integrated Resource Planning (IRP) Process. As part of the business model plan, detailed scenarios considering technological advancements, market trends, policy changes, and consumer behavior would have been developed. An enhanced analysis framework, incorporating advanced modeling techniques and stakeholder engagement, will assess the robustness of each scenario. 5. Implementation Roadmap.
